subject: Embeddings model fit validation — post-demo follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acme-search.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme-search.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 15:10:00 -0000
Subject: Embeddings model fit validation — post-demo follow-up & next steps

Hi Elena / Sam —

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we have alignment: 

1) Summary of pain: your e-commerce relevance team is seeing cold-start problems on product pages and degraded recall for long-tail queries after the last catalog update.
2) What we demonstrated: Redwood embeddings endpoint with batching + prefix caching, plus a quick semantic search demo using 1536-d and 768-d vectors for comparison.
3) Initial observations: 1536-d model (open-1536-v2) had better MRR and recall@10 on the sample set, but higher latency and storage. The 768-d model (open-768-lite) ran ~30% faster with approx -6% MRR on the current prompt set.

Recommended next steps: 
- We’ll run a targeted fit validation over your benchmark (the 4k query set you shared) comparing three model candidates: open-1536-v2, open-768-lite-quant, and a finetuned 1024-d variant we can spin up as a short eval.
- Redwood will provide metrics: MRR, recall@1/5/10, cosine-sim distribution, and drift score over the last 3 catalog snapshots.
- We’ll share a prompt set template + evaluation harness (Drive link attached) and a suggested QA checklist for regression detection.

Can you confirm: (a) approval to run the eval on your 4k dataset, (b) preferred S3/Drive location for results, and (c) any restrictions around PII or retention?

Attaching our quick benchmark export and the evaluation prompt set we usually start with. I’ve cc’d Marissa from Model Ops who’ll own the run.

Thanks — talk soon.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: embeddings-bench-1.csv (sample export), eval-promptset-v2.md
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acme-search.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme-search.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:42:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Embeddings model fit validation — post-demo follow-up & next steps

Hey Marcus —

Appreciate the recap — yes that matches our notes. Couple quick clarifications before we greenlight the eval: 

1) Dataset: the 4k query set contains scraped user queries — it may have some PII fragments (names/emails). We can either mask or sign an appropriate DPA addendum. Do you have a standard masking script or guidance?
2) Drift: we’re especially worried about semantic drift after last month’s taxonomy change. Can you measure per-category drift (we can provide category tags) and show cosine distribution shifts?
3) Dimensionality trade-offs: storage for embeddings is a real cost vector for us. Can you include an approx $/month storage and retrieval cost delta for each dimensionality you test?

If these are doable, please proceed — we prefer results in the S3 bucket acme-search-evals (read/write to the folder /prod/emb-2027-03).

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of Relevance — Acme Search
elena.torres@acme-search.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acme-search.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme-search.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 15:30:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Embeddings model fit validation — post-demo follow-up & next steps

Hi Elena —

All doable. Quick notes on your points: 

1) PII handling: we can run the eval on a masked copy. I’ve attached a lightweight masking script and the promptset includes a masking step. If you prefer DPA-level controls we can escalate to legal, but masking + ephemeral retention (7 days) is our usual pattern for discovery evals.

2) Per-category drift: yes — we’ll compute per-category MRR and delta in cosine distribution across the three most recent catalog snapshots. Output will include the mean/median cosine and a simple drift score (Jensen-Shannon divergence on binned cosine). Attached is a sample covariance-plot.png showing the type of visualization we’ll provide.

3) Cost delta: we’ll include estimated storage and retrieval cost per month for each dimensionality tested (assumptions documented):
   - 1536-d (float16): ~X GB / 1M vectors = ~ $Y/month (index + object storage)
   - 1024-d (float16 quant): ~ ~0.67X GB, savings ~30%
   - 768-d (int8 quant): ~0.5X GB, savings ~50% but expect ~5–8% MRR degradation on long-tail queries (based on our prior benchmarks)

Plan: we’ll run the three-model sweep on your S3 path (acme-search-evals/prod/emb-2027-03) overnight and post results + CSVs into the folder. ETA: 48 hours after you confirm masked dataset or provide S3 creds (temporary IAM role preferred).

Do you want us to spin up the finetuned 1024-d variant or start with the two open models first? Spinning a short finetune costs an extra 4-6 hours and we’ll need a small compute commit.

Next steps: please reply with: (A) confirm masking vs DPA, (B) S3 path + IAM role or upload, (C) approval to include finetune (yes/no).

—Marcus
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 16:05:00 -0000
Subject: Fwd: Embeddings model fit validation — quick internal question

Marcus —

Looping in Rishi is good. For the finetune cost/numbers we should include a short note on dimensionality effects on ANN index sizing (HNSW defaults we use). Can you also add the expected recall/latency curve at 99th pct so customers can weigh SLO impacts? I can draft the cost table after you drop the raw CSVs.

Also: when you upload results, tag the run with HS-ACME-000421 in HubSpot so AE can pick it up.

—Marissa
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acme-search.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme-search.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:25:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Embeddings model fit validation — post-demo follow-up & next steps

Thanks everyone — quick confirmation: 

- Elena: masking is fine; we’ll use your masked copy. Please upload to acme-search-evals/prod/emb-2027-03 and share an IAM role with S3:PutObject/Read for 48 hours.
- Finetune: we’ll run the two open models first (1536 and 768 quant) and if you’re happy we can add the 1024-d finetune in a follow-up sweep (keeps initial cost/time lower).
- Deliverables (by EOD Thu): full CSVs (embeddings-bench-1.csv), per-category MRR + recall tables, cosine distribution plots (covariance-plot.png), and a cost delta sheet. We’ll also include the eval promptset (eval-promptset-v2.md) and a short README for reproducibility.

I’ll set a follow-up call for Friday to walk through results (30 min). Proposed: Fri 2027-04-02 16:00 PT — does that work for you?

Cheers,
Marcus
